documents.unit: Office of Academic Affairs, Faculty Affairs
documents.title: Artificial intelligence and academic integrity
documents.summary: A 2023 Provost-office news item telling students that generative AI is off limits for coursework unless the individual instructor authorizes it. It grounds the rule in the Code of Student Conduct and academic integrity.
documents.stance_why: The statement says generative AI tools 'should not be used in the completion of course assignments unless an instructor for a given course specifically authorizes their use'. That is a default ban lifted only by explicit instructor permission, so restrict rather than delegates, because the default is stated.

units.why: The sentence frames generative AI as shaping "the future of work, research and technology" before warning of misuse; it is a rationale (informs), nearest the career type P44 but it is not a learn-AI-for-careers rule.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P44 with the same fit_note and codes. The sentence says AI 'will help shape the future of work, research and technology', a rationale about AI's importance, not a rule that courses teach AI; P44 kept with the fit note. Topics merged (A: ai-literacy-career; B: learning-rationale, ai-literacy-career).
units.anchor: These tools will help shape the future of work, research and technology
units.fit_note: States AI matters for the future of work, but does not say courses should teach AI use.

units.why: "when used in the wrong way, they can stand in conflict with academic integrity" frames AI misuse as an integrity issue; the reason is honesty, not skill-building, so P95 rather than P41.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P95: 'when used in the wrong way, they can stand in conflict with academic integrity' grounds AI limits in integrity, not skill-building. Codes identical.
units.anchor: when used in the wrong way, they can stand in conflict with academic integrity
units.frag_start: when used in the wrong way

units.why: "complete all academic and scholarly activities with fairness and honesty" binds students under the Code of Student Conduct; the reason given is fairness and honesty, so P95.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. The source says 'All students have important obligations under the Code of Student Conduct to complete all academic and scholarly activities with fairness and honesty', a real obligation whose stated reason is fairness and honesty, so kept as P95. Coder A did not code it.
units.anchor: complete all academic and scholarly activities with fairness and honesty

units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The source says 'Our professional students also have the responsibility to uphold the professional and ethical standards found in their respective academic honor codes', a real obligation tying professional programs to existing honor codes; kept as P77 with A's fit note.
units.anchor: Our professional students also have the responsibility to uphold the professional and ethical standards
units.fit_note: Refers to professional honor codes of programs rather than laws or university-wide policy.

units.why: Students are 'not to use unauthorized assistance in the laboratory, on field work, in scholarship or on a course assignment' unless the instructor authorized it. It is a general integrity rule that AI falls under; P36 fits better than P04 because the focus is the obligation under the Code.
units.resolution_why: Coder A chose P36 (integrity rule under the Code), coder B chose P06 (fallback rule). The source says students are not to use 'unauthorized assistance in the laboratory, on field work, in scholarship or on a course assignment' unless 'authorized specifically by the course instructor'. That states what applies unless the instructor authorizes it, which is P06; it classifies no act as misconduct and names no process, which is what P36 covers. Final: P06 with a fit note. Policy text taken from A because the anchor omits the exception.
units.anchor: unauthorized assistance in the laboratory, on field work, in scholarship or on a course assignment
units.frag_end: authorized specifically by the course instructor.
units.policy: Students may not use unauthorized assistance in the laboratory, on field work, in scholarship or on a course assignment unless the course instructor has specifically authorized it
units.fit_note: Speaks of unauthorized assistance in general; AI is not named in this sentence. A also noted it states the obligation under the Code of Student Conduct but no misconduct classification or process.

units.why: 'students are not to submit their work without acknowledging any word-for-word use and/or paraphrasing of writing, ideas or other work that is not your own' requires acknowledgment of others' work, which the document applies to AI. P24 is nearest but the passage speaks of sources generally, so a fit note.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P24 with a fit note. Modality: A must, B must-not; the sentence is worded 'students are not to submit their work without acknowledging', so must-not follows the text. Unit stance: A restrict, B require; 'require' would mean AI use is required, which the sentence does not say, and acknowledgment is a condition on use, so restrict. A's anchor kept; policy added because the anchor is a fragment.

documents.unit: Code of Student Conduct (Ohio Admin. Code 3335-23-04)
documents.title: Prohibited conduct, 3335-23-04
documents.summary: The Code of Student Conduct rule on prohibited conduct. Only one clause concerns AI, listing unauthorized generative AI use among examples of academic misconduct; related clauses on course rules apply indirectly.
documents.stance_why: Rule (A)(5) makes "Unauthorized use of generative artificial intelligence" academic misconduct, implying AI is banned unless authorized; the rule names no permitted uses, so restrict.

units.why: Clause (A)(5) lists 'Unauthorized use of generative artificial intelligence systems or similar technologies to complete academic activities' as academic misconduct. This classifies unauthorized AI use as misconduct under the Code, so P36; 'unauthorized' means authorized use is not covered.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P36 for Clause (A)(5), 'Unauthorized use of generative artificial intelligence systems or similar technologies to complete academic activities'. Unit stance: A prohibit, B restrict; 'unauthorized' means authorized use is outside the misconduct, so restrict. Policy null (anchor states the rule), as both.
units.anchor: Unauthorized use of generative artificial intelligence systems or similar technologies to complete academic activities

units.why: The opening says any student who engaged 'in any of the following conduct' 'will be subject to disciplinary action by the university', so AI misconduct (item A5) leads to discipline. No specific penalty is named, so P36 not P37.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P36 for 'will be subject to disciplinary action by the university'. Modality: A informs, B must; the sentence states a consequence ('will be subject to') rather than commanding a behavior, so informs. Unit stance neutral (A) since the consequence applies to all listed conduct and takes no AI position of its own (B: restrict). A's normalized policy kept; it adds the AI example from clause (5) and the attempt wording from the source.
units.anchor: will be subject to disciplinary action by the university
units.frag_start: Any student found to have engaged
units.policy: Any student found to have engaged, or attempted to engage, in the listed conduct, including unauthorized use of generative AI to complete academic activities, is subject to disciplinary action by the university

units.why: The rule defines 'attempt' as 'conduct that, if successful, would constitute or result in the prohibited conduct', so attempted unauthorized AI use is also punishable. No type covers attempt liability, so UNCOVERED.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The source says 'attempt shall be defined as conduct that, if successful, would constitute or result in the prohibited conduct', so attempted unauthorized AI use is covered like completed use. A real rule; no type covers attempt liability, so UNCOVERED kept.
units.anchor: attempt shall be defined as conduct that, if successful, would constitute
units.uncovered_note: Attempting prohibited conduct, including unauthorized AI use, is treated the same as completing it.

units.why: Item (A)(1), 'Violation of course rules and/or assignment guidelines as contained in the course syllabus', makes breaking a course's AI rules misconduct. It is not AI-specific but gives instructor-set AI rules their force, so P36.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P36 for (1), 'Violation of course rules and/or assignment guidelines as contained in the course syllabus', which gives syllabus AI rules enforcement force. Codes identical; fit note kept.
units.anchor: Violation of course rules and/or assignment guidelines as contained in the course syllabus
units.fit_note: General rule on course rules and assignment guidelines; AI is not named.

units.why: Item (A)(12), 'Violation of program regulations and/or policies as established by departmental committees', extends misconduct to program rules, which would cover departmental AI rules. P85 is closest in subject but the item is about enforcement, so P36.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The source lists (12) 'Violation of program regulations and/or policies as established by departmental committees and made available to students' as academic misconduct, so departmental AI rules are enforceable. A real rule, P36 as in clause (1); fit note kept.
units.anchor: Violation of program regulations and/or policies as established by departmental committees
units.fit_note: General rule on departmental program regulations; AI is not named.

units.why: Under (N), 'Students are responsible for reviewing and undertstanding the rules, standards and guidelines provided to them by their academic programs and colleges' puts the duty to learn local rules (here including AI rules) on students. That is P78.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P78, course-start, must, for 'Students are responsible for reviewing and undertstanding the rules, standards and guidelines provided to them by their academic programs and colleges'. Codes identical; A's topics kept (adds accountability-understanding).
units.anchor: Students are responsible for reviewing and undertstanding the rules, standards and guidelines

notes: Reconciled from coders A and B. All three documents are restrict. The AI paragraph of the Provost notice repeats verbatim in the Recommended Syllabus Statements, so it is coded in each document. Several units are general integrity rules with no AI named; fit notes kept. No college or computing-unit policy found; course layer deferred. Non-AI syllabus statements (content warning, counseling, disability, copyright, etc.) were skipped by both coders.
